reason: Both describe the identical mechanism at the identical location: the functional setState updater (setSets(s => ...)) calls stateFor(lift)/fn(stateFor(lift)) which reads the prior set list from the outer-scope `sets` closure rather than from its own `s` parameter. Both describe the same consequence: two same-lift taps queued in one React batch each read the same stale snapshot, so the second updater's write clobbers the first's, silently dropping an edit. The reviewer's finding is a detailed paraphrase (even naming the same `sets[keyFor(lift.id)] ?? seedFor(lift)` definition) of the ground-truth mechanism, not a different bug or vague complaint.
